name: Clozapine
route_note: Oral tablets, orally disintegrating tablets or suspension, titrated slowly with blood count monitoring.

discovery.note: Synthesised in 1958–59 as a tricyclic dibenzodiazepine; it was unusual in having antipsychotic effects without catalepsy in animals.

tagline: Uniquely effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia
summary: Clozapine is the prototype atypical antipsychotic and the only drug with proven superiority in treatment-resistant schizophrenia; it also reduces suicidal behaviour. It was withdrawn in the 1970s after deaths from agranulocytosis and reintroduced in 1989 with mandatory blood monitoring.
mechanism: Clozapine has relatively weak and transient dopamine D2 receptor occupancy combined with potent 5-HT2A antagonism, a profile linked to its very low risk of extrapyramidal effects and tardive dyskinesia. It also binds D4, 5-HT2C, muscarinic, histamine and adrenergic receptors.
Its metabolite N-desmethylclozapine is a muscarinic M1 partial agonist. Why clozapine works where other antipsychotics fail is not fully understood.
uses: Reducing risk of recurrent suicidal behaviour in schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Clozapine is marketed in Europe as Leponex.

history.title: Finnish deaths
history.detail: Agranulocytosis deaths in Finland lead to withdrawal or restriction in many countries.

history.title: Kane trial
history.detail: John Kane's multicentre trial shows superiority over chlorpromazine in treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Clozaril (Sandoz) is approved in the US with mandatory white blood cell monitoring.

history.title: Suicide indication
history.detail: Based on the InterSePT trial, the FDA approves clozapine for reducing suicidal behaviour.

history.title: Clozapine REMS
history.detail: The FDA consolidates monitoring registries into a single Clozapine REMS using absolute neutrophil count.

history.title: REMS ended
history.detail: The FDA eliminates the Clozapine REMS, no longer requiring pharmacies to verify blood test results before dispensing.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic, mainly CYP1A2 (also 2D6, 3A4); levels fall with smoking

safety.boxed_warning: Severe neutropenia; orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia and syncope; seizures; myocarditis and cardiomyopathy; increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.

facts: Stopping smoking can raise clozapine levels markedly because tobacco smoke induces CYP1A2.
Clozapine is the only antipsychotic approved specifically to reduce suicidal behaviour.
